So you bought cashmere…and now it’s pilling? 🧶 Don’t panic.
Pilling is a normal part of owning cashmere you just need to know how to care for it.
Here’s how to remove cashmere pilling safely and keep your knitwear looking its best.

🔗 you can comment CASHMERE for the list of products used in this video or head to my bio
items.transcript: Cashmere is one of my favorite, favorite fabrics. And if there's a staple that I would suggest anyone had in their wardrobe, I'd tell you a cashmere jumper is exactly that. It should be something that lasts for years and years, and you can wear over and over again. If I was still working on the shop floor and I was selling you a cashmere jumper, there would be a couple of things that I would advise you to buy and also a couple of pieces of advice that I would give you about ownership and upkeep. So first of all, let's talk about pilling. I want to show you the pilling on this jumper. Pilling is completely normal. It's just where the fibers are rubbing together and creating these little balls. You can see this jumper is free of pilling around the neck. That's because my coat is often open, so there's not much friction to be had around my neck. But you can see under my arm, there's lots because I'm constantly moving and all that pilling is happening in those areas where there's lots of movement. So let's talk about how to depill your cashmere. There's two things that I would encourage my customers to purchase. The first is a cashmere comb. This is great for people who are going to commit to that very regular maintenance and it will easily get the smaller pills off and is very gentle on the fabric. The second is much more convenient. It's a fabric shaver and this will help you do larger areas in a quicker amount of time and also catch those larger pills that your fabric comb isn't quite getting off. So what I'm saying is don't panic when your lovely new cashmere starts to bobble. It doesn't mean you've made a bad purchase. It doesn't mean it's low quality and it certainly doesn't mean that you should be returning it. Sometimes there's nothing wrong with what you bought. You just weren't told what ownership looks like. If you've got any questions, let me know.

It's going to be done and you're going to know how to do it for the future. And your £500 coffee machine is going to continue to give you after value because you're maintaining it the way you should. First things first I'm going to show you the state of mine. I'm going to clean all of this because what collects is the bits of coffee and then oils. You should find that if you've left this a long time the next coffee that you have afterwards tastes a little bit fresher. Before we start a couple of things that you'll need. I want you to go and look for this box. You got this when you purchased the coffee machine. Inside here is the tablet that we're going to use to clean this section of the coffee machine. Next you need to find this little cleaning tray here. Now this is going to hold the tablet and stop the water from filtering through when we clean the coffee machine. The last thing you need to check before you start the clean is that this has the double basket on. If you're not sure where it is it might again be sat in your accessory cupboard. Just be careful when you take it out because sometimes it does have a little bit of water in and it is hot. So be very careful. Then you're going to take this out like that and then we can do the rest of our cleaning. So we're going to empty the water tray because as you can see it is completely full. To finish off we need to make sure we put this back in our accessory covered and as you can see I've given it a nice clean. That just took a few minutes as well, nothing major. items.caption: Which use tissue to fold my clothes
items.transcript: Okay, let's talk about why I use tissue paper to fold my clothes. Now the first part of the answer is quite simply habit. From working in retail for so many years, folding clothes with tissue paper is just ingrained into my soul. However, there is a really practical reason why I still use this technique that translates really nicely from the shop floor to our homes. I fold the tissue paper to size judged on the type of storage that I'm going to use. So then instead of trying to judge where to fold the knitwear, I use the tissue paper as my guide. Sleeves in, fold around the paper, and every single one comes out pretty much the exact same size. So yes, the tissue paper does look really aesthetically pleasing, but the main thing is it saves me time because I'm doing the right fold first time. And yes, I do use the same piece of tissue paper over and over and over and over and over and over again.
